_comment: Single source of truth for every figure that appears on screen. The HTML rebuild reads these, and the same values must be seeded into the app before recording capture-scan-flow, so the rebuilt frames and the real device capture cannot disagree. Persona is the launch beachhead from PipComp/docs/business-plan.md: a young Malaysian professional with real income who still does not know where it goes.

headline._comment: Frame 3's payoff. Deliberately POSITIVE. The emotional beat of the video cannot be a red overspent number.

sourceScreen._comment: The generic look-alike e-wallet in Frame 1. NEUTRAL BY DESIGN: no brand name, no logo, no real trademarks. This is commercial marketing on a paid store listing, so it must read as 'an e-wallet' without being anyone's actual product. Recognition comes from the shape of the list and the RM amounts, not from a mark.

lift._comment: Frame 2 choreography. Rows leave the source ONE AT A TIME so the eye can follow a single row through its whole journey. r1 carries the 'learned' badge because it is the proof of the differentiator: Pip remembers merchants, so categorizing gets faster the more you use it. Exactly ONE chip resolves in brand green (r1, Food) and it is one of the video's three permitted accent uses.

categoryColors._comment: Computed from PipComp/src/lib/catColors.ts at the hues in PipComp/src/data/categories.ts. bg = oklch(0.95 0.045 h), fg = oklch(0.52 0.13 h), solid = oklch(0.60 0.13 h). Real UI colour, NOT brand accent, and does not count against the three-uses rule.

_captionsComment: Absolute seconds, as actually built. Caption 3 arrives AFTER the number resolves rather than racing it, so one subject moves at a time. That leaves 2.25s of held silence at the end of frame 3.

captions.text: Screenshot what you already have open.
